title: Retro-orbital Injection of Virus or Dye in Mice
author: Boaz Mohar
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.5udg6s6

steps.title: Prepare Injection Material
steps.instruction: Prepare the virus dilution (5.0e11-1.0e12) with PBS or a dye aliquot.

steps.title: Induce Anesthesia
steps.instruction: Anesthetize the mouse using isoflurane in two stages.

substeps.instruction: Place mouse in an induction chamber with isoflurane at 3% and a flow rate of ~1L/min.
Once breathing slows to ~1/s, move the mouse to a nose cone delivery of isoflurane at 1.5% with the same flow rate.

steps.title: Expose the Eyeball
steps.instruction: Expose the eyeball using two fingers (above and below), ensuring no pressure is applied to the trachea and breathing remains regular.

steps.title: Perform Retro-orbital Injection
steps.instruction: Inject up to 200ul of material using a 29G x 12.7mm 0.3ml syringe (Ulticare Catalog #09230).

substeps.instruction: Insert the needle at a 30-degree angle, beveled downwards, until the bone is hit.
Retract the needle slightly and inject slowly.

steps.title: Post-Injection Care
steps.instruction: Remove the needle slowly and press the eyelid shut for a few seconds.

steps.title: Validate Injection Success
steps.instruction: If using JF525, verify the injection by checking the animal's urine after it wakes up.

substeps.instruction: Place the animal in a clean cup with kim-wips to collect urine; successful injection is indicated by pink urine.
